ask.why: The lower-left element of the system matrix equals minus the equivalent power.

steps.note: The equivalent focal length of the two lenses in air.

ask.q: What happens to \(1/F\) when \(d = f_1 + f_2\) (a telescope)?
ask.why: With \(d = f_1 + f_2\), the \(dP_1P_2\) term cancels the sum, giving an afocal system.

cards.q: If two thin lenses of focal lengths \( f_1 \) and \( f_2 \) are separated by a medium of refractive index \( n \) and thickness \( d \), the equivalent focal length satisfies \( 1/F \) equal to ____.
cards.why: Replacing d by the reduced distance \(d/n\) gives \(1/F = 1/f1 + 1/f2 - d/(n f1 f2)\).

cards.q: In Ramsden's and Huygens' eyepieces, two converging lenses are separated by a suitable distance \( d \) to minimize ____.
cards.why: Setting \(d = (f1 + f2)/2\) makes the two-lens combination achromatic for all wavelengths.

cards.q: The condition for achromatism of two thin lenses made of the same glass and separated by distance \( d \) in air is \( d \) equal to ____.
cards.why: Differentiating \(1/F\) with respect to n gives \(d = (f1 + f2)/2\) for identical glass.

sheets.title: Q22 · Definition and explanation of polarization (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 22
cards.q: Define and explain polarization.
Definition of polarization, unpolarized vs polarized light, and transverse nature

options.t: Confinement/asymmetry of electric field vibrations perpendicular to propagation direction defined, unpolarized vs plane/circular/elliptical polarized light explained with diagrams, and transverse wave proof noted
Definition and basic description without diagrams or transverse wave explanation

cards.why: Define polarization of electromagnetic waves, contrast unpolarized and polarized light, and explain how it proves light is transverse.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Polarization of light and transverse wave nature
cards.body: Know first: Polarisation: introduction and transverse wave nature (17). Polarization is the phenomenon of restricting the vibrations of the transverse electric field vector \( \mathbf{E} \) of a light wave to a specific orientation or regular path in the plane perpendicular to the direction of propagation \( \mathbf{k} \). In ordinary unpolarized light (from the sun or a lamp), the direction of \( \mathbf{E} \) in the transverse \( x\text{-}y \) plane changes randomly every \( \sim 10^{-8}\text{ s} \). When passed through a polarizer (like a Polaroid or tourmaline crystal), \( \mathbf{E} \) oscillates along a single fixed line (linearly polarized light). Because longitudinal waves are symmetrical about their propagation axis, polarization conclusively proves that light waves are transverse.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Transverse electromagnetic wave equations
cards.tex: \text{Unpolarized: } E_x(t), E_y(t) \text{ have random relative phase; } E_z = 0 \\ \text{x-polarized: } E_x = E_0\cos(kz - \omega t), \quad E_y = 0, \quad E_z = 0 \\ \text{Malus's law after analyzer at angle } \theta: \quad I = I_0\cos^2\theta
cards.body: Define polarization, contrast random unpolarized vibrations with restricted polarized vibrations using diagrams, and explain the proof of transverse character. Definition 1.5 · unpolarized vs polarized & diagrams 1.5 · transverse nature 1.

cards.q: The phenomenon of polarization proves conclusively that light waves are ____.
cards.why: Only transverse waves have directional asymmetry about the line of propagation.

cards.q: In a plane electromagnetic light wave, the optical effects (and polarization direction) are identified with the ____.
cards.why: The electric vector E exerts the primary force on electrons in matter and detectors.

cards.q: Sound waves in air cannot be polarized because they are ____.
cards.why: Longitudinal displacements are along the direction of propagation, so rotating a slit does not block them.

sheets.title: Q23 · Distinction between positive and negative uniaxial crystals (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 23
cards.q: Distinguish between positive uniaxial and negative uniaxial crystals.
Comparison of refractive indices, wave speeds, Huygens wavefronts, and examples

options.t: Four points compared: (1) ne > no vs ne < no, (2) vo > ve vs vo < ve, (3) ellipsoid inside sphere vs outside sphere (with diagrams), and (4) examples (quartz vs calcite)

cards.why: Compare refractive indices, velocities, wavefront geometry, and examples for positive and negative uniaxial crystals.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Positive vs negative uniaxial crystals
cards.body: Know first: Double refraction and Huygens' explanation (20). (1) Refractive index: In a positive uniaxial crystal, \( n_e > n_o \) (birefringence \( n_e - n_o > 0 \)); in a negative uniaxial crystal, \( n_e < n_o \) (\( n_e - n_o < 0 \)). (2) Wave velocity: Off the optic axis, \( v_o > v_e \) in a positive crystal (e-ray is slow), whereas \( v_e > v_o \) in a negative crystal (e-ray is fast). (3) Huygens wave surfaces: The e-ray ellipsoid of revolution lies inside the o-ray sphere in a positive crystal, and outside the o-ray sphere in a negative crystal (both touching along the optic axis). (4) Examples: Quartz and ice are positive; calcite and tourmaline are negative.
cards.tex: \text{Positive: } n_e > n_o,\; v_o > v_e \text{ (Quartz)}; \quad \text{Negative: } n_e < n_o,\; v_e > v_o \text{ (Calcite)}

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Summary comparison of uniaxial crystals
cards.tex: \text{1. Index: } \text{Positive: } n_e > n_o; \quad \text{Negative: } n_e < n_o \\ \text{2. Velocity } (\theta = \pi/2): \quad \text{Positive: } v_e = \frac{c}{n_e} < v_o = \frac{c}{n_o}; \quad \text{Negative: } v_e = \frac{c}{n_e} > v_o = \frac{c}{n_o} \\ \text{3. Wavefronts: Positive: ellipsoid inside sphere; Negative: ellipsoid outside sphere} \\ \text{4. Examples: Positive: quartz, ice, rutile; Negative: calcite, tourmaline, ruby}
cards.body: Contrast refractive indices, velocities, wavefront shapes (with sketches), and crystal examples. Four comparison points 4.

cards.q: In a positive uniaxial crystal, the extraordinary ray is refracted ____.
options: more than the ordinary ray (closer to the normal)
cards.why: Because \(n_e > n_o\) in a positive crystal, the e-ray bends more towards the normal than the o-ray.

cards.q: In both positive and negative uniaxial crystals, the number of optic axes is ____.
cards.why: Uniaxial crystals have a single optic axis direction along which \(v_o = v_e\).

cards.q: Crystals like mica and topaz that have two directions along which the two rays travel at equal speed are called ____.
cards.why: As noted in the footnote on page 22.15 of Ghatak, crystals with two optic axes are biaxial.

sheets.title: Q24 · Critical angle of an optical fiber and its expression (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 24
cards.q: What is meant by critical angle of an optical fiber ? Obtain an expression for the critical angle.
Definition of critical angle at the core-cladding interface

options.t: Minimum angle of incidence in the denser core (n1) for which the angle of refraction in the rarer cladding (n2) is 90 degrees, above which total internal reflection occurs

cards.why: Define the critical angle at the core-cladding boundary and its role in total internal reflection.

cards.q: Ray diagram and derivation of \(\theta_c = \sin^{-1}(n2 / n1)\)

options.t: Diagram and Snell's law derivation \(n1 \sin \theta_c = n2 \sin 90 = n2 => \theta_c = \sin^{-1}(n2/n1)\)

cards.why: Apply Snell's law at the core-cladding interface with angle of refraction \(r = 90\) degrees.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Critical angle of an optical fiber
cards.body: Know first: Laws of reflection and refraction from Fermat's principle. The critical angle \( \theta_c \) of an optical fiber is the angle of incidence inside the denser core (refractive index \( n_1 \)) at the core-cladding boundary for which the refracted ray in the rarer cladding (refractive index \( n_2 < n_1 \)) grazes the interface at \( r = 90^\circ \). Applying Snell's law \( n_1\sin\theta_c = n_2\sin 90^\circ \) gives \( \sin\theta_c = \frac{n_2}{n_1} \), or \( \theta_c = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{n_2}{n_1}\right) \). Rays with \( \theta_i > \theta_c \) undergo total internal reflection.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Derivation of critical angle expression
cards.tex: \text{Snell's law at core-cladding interface: } n_1\sin\theta_i = n_2\sin\theta_r \\ \text{At critical angle } (\theta_i = \theta_c,\; \theta_r = 90^\circ): \quad n_1\sin\theta_c = n_2\sin 90^\circ = n_2 \\ \sin\theta_c = \frac{n_2}{n_1} \implies \theta_c = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{n_2}{n_1}\right) \\ \cos\theta_c = \frac{\sqrt{n_1^2 - n_2^2}}{n_1} = \frac{\text{NA}}{n_1}
cards.body: Define the critical angle, draw the core-cladding grazing refraction ray, and set \(\theta_r = 90\) degrees in Snell's law. Definition 2 · diagram & derivation 2.

cards.label: Derivation
cards.title: Critical angle at the core-cladding interface, step by step
cards.legend: A ray in the core \(n_1\) meets the cladding \(n_2 < n_1\) at the critical angle \(\theta_c\), and the refracted ray grazes the boundary at \(90^\circ\).

phases.why: the law at the core-cladding surface

phases.name: Grazing refraction r = 90 deg

phases.why: solve for theta c

ask.q: Why must \(n_1\) be greater than \(n_2\) for a real critical angle?
ask.why: \(\sin\theta_c = n_2/n_1\) has a solution only when this ratio is less than one.

steps.note: At the threshold, the refracted ray grazes the boundary.

ask.q: What happens to the ray in the core when \(\theta_i > \theta_c\)?
ask.why: Beyond the critical angle there is no refracted ray, so all light is reflected.

steps.note: Use \(\sin 90^\circ = 1\) and divide by \(n_1\).

ask.q: For a core of index 1.48 and cladding 1.46, \(\theta_c\) is close to:
ask.why: \(\sin\theta_c = 1.46/1.48 \approx 0.986\), so \(\theta_c\) is about 80 degrees.

steps.note: Then \(n_1\cos\theta_c = \sqrt{n_1^2 - n_2^2}\), the numerical aperture.

ask.q: What is the refraction angle in the cladding when \(\theta_i = \theta_c\)?
ask.why: At the critical angle the refracted ray grazes the boundary.

cards.q: If a fiber has \( n_1 = 1.50 \) and \( n_2 = 1.47 \), the sine of its critical angle \( \sin\theta_c \) is ____.
In terms of the critical angle \( \theta_c \), the maximum angle \( \theta_{\text{axis}} \) that a guided meridional ray can make with the fiber axis inside the core is ____.
cards.why: The normal to the wall is perpendicular to the fiber axis, so \(\theta_{axis} = 90 - \theta_c\).

cards.q: In terms of core index \( n_1 \) and critical angle \( \theta_c \), the numerical aperture in air is ____.
cards.why: NA = \(n1 \sin(90 - \theta_c) = n1 \cos(\theta_c) = \sqrt{n1^2 - n2^2}\).

sheets.title: Q25 · Wavelength absent in reflected light from a soap film (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 25
cards.q: A soap film \(5 \times 10^{-5}\) cm thick is viewed at an angle of \(35^{\circ}\) to the normal. Find the wavelength of light in the visible spectrum which will be absent from the reflected light. Given \(\mu = 1.33\) ?
Calculation of \(\cos r\) from Snell's law and destructive wavelengths \(\lambda = 2 \mu d \cos r / m\)

options.t: \(\cos r = 0.9003\), \(2 \mu d \cos r = 1.197\times 10^{-4}\) cm, and visible absent wavelength for \(m = 2\) is 5987 A (or for \(m = 3\) is 3991 A)
Used \(i = 35\) deg as r instead of applying Snell's law
Destructive condition \(2 \mu d \cos r = m \lambda\) stated only

cards.why: Find \(\sin r = \sin\)(35 deg) / 1.33, compute \(2 \mu d \cos r\), and divide by integer m to find the wavelength in the visible range \((4000 A - 7000 A)\).

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Absent visible wavelength \(\lambda = 5987\) A (for \(m = 2\))
cards.body: Know first: Colours of thin films, Newton's rings, Michelson interferometer (11). By Snell's law, \( \sin r = \frac{\sin 35^\circ}{1.33} = \frac{0.5736}{1.33} = 0.4313 \), so \( \cos r = \sqrt{1 - 0.4313^2} = 0.9022 \). For a wavelength to be absent (destructive interference) in reflected light, \( 2\mu d\cos r = m\lambda \). With \( d = 5\times 10^{-5}\text{ cm} \) and \( \mu = 1.33 \), \( 2\mu d\cos r = 1.200\times 10^{-4}\text{ cm} = 12000\text{ \AA} \). For \( m = 1, 2, 3 \), \( \lambda = 12000\text{ \AA}, 6000\text{ \AA}, 4000\text{ \AA} \); thus \( \lambda_2 = 6000\text{ \AA} \) (and \( \lambda_3 = 4000\text{ \AA} \) at the violet edge) is absent in the visible spectrum.

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Calculation of destructive interference wavelength
cards.tex: d = 5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ cm}, \quad i = 35^\circ, \quad \mu = 1.33 \\ \sin r = \frac{\sin 35^\circ}{1.33} = \frac{0.5736}{1.33} = 0.4313 \implies \cos r = \sqrt{1 - 0.4313^2} = 0.9022 \\ \text{Destructive condition in reflected light: } 2\mu d\cos r = m\lambda \\ 2\mu d\cos r = 2 \times 1.33 \times 5 \times 10^{-5} \times 0.9022 = 1.200 \times 10^{-4}\text{ cm} = 12000\text{ \AA} \\ m = 1: \lambda_1 = 12000\text{ \AA (IR)}; \quad m = 2: \lambda_2 = 6000\text{ \AA (Visible)}; \quad m = 3: \lambda_3 = 4000\text{ \AA (Violet edge)}
cards.body: Find \(\cos r\) using Snell's law, evaluate \(2 \mu d \cos r = 12000\) A, and test integer values \(m = 1\), 2, 3 to select the wavelength inside the visible spectrum (4000–7000 A). \(\cos r\) calculation 1.5 · \(2 \mu d \cos r = m \lambda 1.5\) · visible selection 1.

cards.q: For a wavelength \( \lambda \) to be absent (dark) in light reflected from a soap film in air, the condition is ____.
cards.why: Because of the \(\pi\) phase shift at the top surface, \(2 \mu d \cos(r) = m \lambda\) gives destructive interference.

cards.q: The visible spectrum of light extends approximately from ____.
cards.why: Human vision spans roughly 4000 A (violet) to 7000 A (red).

cards.q: When light enters a soap film of refractive index \( \mu = 1.33 \) from air at \( i = 35^\circ \), the angle of refraction \( r \) is determined from ____.
cards.why: By Snell's law, \(1 \cdot \sin(i) = \mu \cdot \sin(r)\).

sheets.title: Q27 · Thickness of quarter-wave and half-wave plates for lambda = 590 nm (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 27
cards.q: Calculate the thickness of (i) quarter wave plate (ii) a half wave plate. Given that \(\mu_0 = 1.973\), \(\mu_e = 2.656\) and \(\lambda = 590\)nm.
Quarter-wave plate and half-wave plate thicknesses

options.t: \(t_{QWP} = 2.16\times 10^{-7}\) m (0.216 um) and \(t_{HWP} = 4.32\times 10^{-7}\) m (0.432 um) calculated

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: (i) QWP = 0.216 um; (ii) HWP = 0.432 um
cards.body: Know first: Quarter-wave and half-wave plates (21). With \( \lambda = 590\text{ nm} = 5.90\times 10^{-7}\text{ m} \) and \( \mu_e - \mu_o = 2.656 - 1.973 = 0.683 \): (i) the thickness of the quarter-wave plate is \( t_{\text{QWP}} = \frac{\lambda}{4(\mu_e - \mu_o)} = \frac{5.90\times 10^{-7}}{4 \times 0.683} = 2.160\times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 0.216\text{ }\mu\text{m} \); (ii) the thickness of the half-wave plate is \( t_{\text{HWP}} = \frac{\lambda}{2(\mu_e - \mu_o)} = 4.319\times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 0.432\text{ }\mu\text{m} \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Calculation of QWP and HWP thicknesses
cards.body: Compute the birefringence \(\mu_e - \mu_o = 0.683\) and evaluate the QWP and HWP thickness formulas. (i) QWP 2 · (ii) HWP 2.

cards.q: Because a single-order quarter-wave plate is often extremely thin and fragile, practical wave plates are frequently made with thickness equal to an ____.
options: odd multiple \((2m + 1)\) of the minimum QWP thickness
even multiple 2m of the QWP thickness
cards.why: As shown in Eq. (22.53) of Ghatak, \(d = (2m + 1) \lambda / [4|n_o - n_e|]\) gives a multi-order QWP.

cards.q: If a crystal plate has thickness equal to an even multiple of \( \lambda / |n_o - n_e| \) (a full-wave plate), the state of polarization of the emergent beam is ____.
options: identical to that of the incident beam
cards.why: A phase difference of \(2m \pi\) leaves the polarization state unchanged.

cards.q: A crystal with \( \mu_o = 1.973 \) and \( \mu_e = 2.656 \) (such as calomel or rutile) has very large ____.
cards.why: \(\mu_e - \mu_o = +0.683\) is a large positive birefringence.

sheets.title: Q29 · Acceptance angle of an optical fiber from core and cladding indices (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 29
cards.q: Calculate the angle of acceptance of a given optical fiber, if the refractive indices of the core and the cladding are 1.563 and 1.498 respectively.
Calculation of NA = \(\sqrt{n1^2 - n2^2}\) and acceptance angle \(\theta_a = \sin^{-1}\)(NA)

options.t: NA = 0.4461 and acceptance angle \(\theta_a = 26.49\) degrees calculated

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Acceptance angle \(\theta_a = 26.49\) degrees (26 deg 29')
cards.body: Know first: Laws of reflection and refraction from Fermat's principle. With \( n_1 = 1.563 \) and \( n_2 = 1.498 \), the numerical aperture is \( \text{NA} = \sqrt{n_1^2 - n_2^2} = \sqrt{1.563^2 - 1.498^2} = \sqrt{2.442969 - 2.244004} = \sqrt{0.198965} = 0.4461 \). The acceptance angle is \( \theta_a = \sin^{-1}(0.4461) = 26.49^\circ \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Calculation of NA and acceptance angle
cards.body: Compute NA = \(\sqrt{n1^2 - n2^2}\) and take the inverse sine to find the acceptance angle. NA calculation 2 · acceptance angle 2.

cards.q: If an optical fiber is placed in water (\( n_0 = 1.33 \)) instead of air (\( n_0 = 1 \)), its acceptance angle \( \theta_a = \sin^{-1}(\text{NA}/n_0) \) ____.
cards.why: Dividing NA by \(n0 = 1.33\) reduces \(\sin(\theta_a)\), so the acceptance cone narrows in water.

cards.q: For \( n_1 = 1.563 \) and \( n_2 = 1.498 \), the critical angle \( \theta_c = \sin^{-1}(n_2/n_1) \) at the core-cladding wall is ____.
A meridional ray is a ray that passes through the ____.
options: central axis of the optical fiber
cards.why: Meridional rays lie in a plane containing the fiber axis and intersect the axis after every reflection.

sheets.title: Q30 · Polarization angle and angle of refraction of water from critical angle (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 30
cards.q: The critical angle of incidence for total reflection in case of water is \(48^{\circ}\). What is its polarization angle ? What is the angle of refraction corresponding to the polarization angle ?
Refractive index \(n = 1/\sin\)(48 deg), polarization angle \(\theta_p = \tan^{-1}(n)\), and refraction angle \(r = 90 - \theta_p\)

options.t: \(n = 1.346\), polarization angle \(\theta_p = 53.38\) deg (53 deg 23'), and refraction angle \(r = 36.62\) deg (36 deg 37') calculated

cards.why: Find \(n = 1 / \sin\)(48 deg) = 1.346, then \(\theta_p = \tan^{-1}(n) = 53.38\) deg and \(r = 90\) deg - \(\theta_p = 36.62\) deg.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: \(\theta_p = 53.38\) degrees and \(r = 36.62\) degrees
cards.body: Know first: Production of linearly polarised light (18). From the critical angle \( \theta_c = 48^\circ \), the refractive index of water is \( n = \frac{1}{\sin 48^\circ} = \frac{1}{0.7431} = 1.3456 \). By Brewster's law, the polarization angle is \( \theta_p = \tan^{-1}(n) = \tan^{-1}(1.3456) = 53.38^\circ \) (\( 53^\circ 23' \)). Since \( \theta_p + r = 90^\circ \), the corresponding angle of refraction is \( r = 90^\circ - 53.38^\circ = 36.62^\circ \) (\( 36^\circ 37' \)).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Calculation of n, Brewster angle, and refraction angle
cards.tex: \theta_c = 48^\circ \implies n = \frac{1}{\sin\theta_c} = \frac{1}{\sin 48^\circ} = \frac{1}{0.74314} = 1.3456 \\ \text{Polarization angle (Brewster's law): } \tan\theta_p = n = 1.3456 \implies \theta_p = \tan^{-1}(1.3456) = 53.38^\circ \; (53^\circ 23') \\ \text{Angle of refraction: } \theta_p + r = 90^\circ \implies r = 90^\circ - 53.38^\circ = 36.62^\circ \; (36^\circ 37')
cards.body: Calculate n from the critical angle, apply Brewster's law for \(\theta_p\), and subtract from 90 degrees for the refraction angle r. Refractive index n 1.5 · polarization angle 1.5 · refraction angle r 1.

cards.q: How is the refractive index \( n \) of a medium related to its critical angle \( \theta_c \) in air?
cards.why: At the critical angle, \(n \sin(\theta_c) = 1 \cdot \sin\)(90 deg) = 1.

cards.q: Combining \( n = 1/\sin\theta_c \) and Brewster's law \( \tan\theta_p = n \) gives the relation ____.
cards.why: Both expressions equal the refractive index n of the medium.

cards.q: For air-water interface (\( n \approx 1.33 \)), the Brewster polarizing angle is approximately ____.
cards.why: As noted in Section 22.3.2 of Ghatak, \(\tan^{-1}(1.33)\) ~ 53 degrees.

sheets.title: Q31 · Wavelength from single-slit Fraunhofer first minimum (4 marks)

cards.label: PYQ · 4 marks
cards.title: Question 31
cards.q: In Fraunhoffer diffraction pattern due to a narrow slit a screen is placed 2m away from the lens to obtain the pattern. If the slit width is 0.2 mm and the first minimum lie 5mm on either sides of the central maximum, find the wavelength of light.
First minimum formula \(b \sin \theta = \lambda (x1 = f \lambda / b)\) and numerical wavelength

options.t: Formula \(\lambda = b x1 / D\) and \(\lambda = 5\times 10^{-7}\) m (500 nm or 5000 A)
Correct formula with unit conversion error

cards.why: Use \(b \sin(\theta) = b (x1 / D) = \lambda\) with \(b = 0.2\) mm, \(x1 = 5\) mm, and \(D = 2\) m.

cards.label: Answer
cards.title: Wavelength \(\lambda = 500\) nm (5000 A)
cards.body: Know first: Single-slit Fraunhofer diffraction pattern (12). For the first minimum (\( m = 1 \)) of a single slit of width \( b = 0.2\text{ mm} = 2\times 10^{-4}\text{ m} \), \( b\sin\theta_1 = \lambda \). Since \( \sin\theta_1 \approx \frac{x_1}{D} \) with \( x_1 = 5\text{ mm} = 5\times 10^{-3}\text{ m} \) and \( D = 2\text{ m} \), the wavelength is \( \lambda = \frac{b x_1}{D} = \frac{2\times 10^{-4} \times 5\times 10^{-3}}{2} = 5\times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 500\text{ nm} = 5000\text{ \AA} \).

cards.label: Solution
cards.title: Calculation of wavelength from first minimum
cards.tex: b = 0.2\text{ mm} = 2 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}, \quad x_1 = 5\text{ mm} = 5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}, \quad D = 2\text{ m} \\ b\sin\theta_1 = \lambda \quad \text{and} \quad \sin\theta_1 \approx \frac{x_1}{D} \\ \lambda = \frac{b x_1}{D} = \frac{2 \times 10^{-4} \times 5 \times 10^{-3}}{2} = 5 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 500\text{ nm} = 5000\text{ \AA}
cards.body: Convert b and x1 to meters and evaluate \(\lambda = b x1 / D\). Formula 1.5 · substitution 1 · result with units 1.5.

cards.q: If the first minimum lies \( 5\text{ mm} \) on either side of the central maximum, the total linear width of the central maximum is ____.
cards.why: The central maximum extends from -x1 to +x1, so its full width is \(2\times1 = 10\) mm.

cards.q: In single-slit Fraunhofer diffraction, the angular position \( \theta_1 \) of the first minimum satisfies ____.
cards.why: Setting \(\beta = \pi b \sin(\theta1) / \lambda = \pi\) gives \(b \sin(\theta1) = \lambda\).

cards.q: In single-slit diffraction, if the screen distance \( D \) is halved, the distance \( x_1 \) of the first minimum from the center ____.
cards.why: \(x1 = D \lambda / b\) is directly proportional to D.
